resumen: The curl with palms facing down. Far less weight moves than in the normal one, and it is not for lack of biceps.
ejecucion: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing back.
Curl up without rotating the wrist: the palm still faces down at the top.
The upper arm stays against your side.
Lower slowly until the arm is fully straight.
Use considerably less weight than in the normal curl: it does not hold the same here.
matices: With the palm down the biceps loses mechanical advantage — part of its job is turning the forearm up — and the weight is mostly held by the muscles underneath and in the forearm. In the grip study, supinated excited the biceps most; pronated, least.
